Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verses 1–2:

The discussion of the words of God, exalted is He: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ (1) ﴿Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?﴾ (2)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: We have already explained the meaning of God's words, exalted is He: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ and mentioned the opinions of the people of interpretation (ta'wil) concerning its interpretation. The view that is closest to correctness among them, in our judgment, is supported by its evidences in what has passed, which suffices without repeating it in this place.

As for His words: ﴿Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?﴾ its meaning is: Do those among your companions, O Muhammad, who went out, thinking that because of the harm of the polytheists toward them, We would leave them without examination or trial (ibtila', imtihan), merely because they said: "We believe in you, O Muhammad, and we affirm what you have brought us from God"? No! Rather, We will test them, so that the truthful among them may be distinguished from the liar.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿We believe, and they will not be tested﴾ he said: They are tried in their selves and their wealth.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and they will not be tested﴾ meaning: they will not be tried.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammil narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hashim, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and they will not be tested﴾ he said: They will not be tried.

As for the first (أن يتركوا), it is in the accusative governed by the verb "ahasiba" (thought). The second (أن يقولوا), according to some grammarians of Arabic, is in the accusative by dependence on "yutraku" (left alone) before it, and the meaning of the sentence, according to His words ﴿Do people think that they will be left alone﴾, is "because they say, 'We believe'"; so when the preposition lam (meaning "because of") was removed from li-anna, it became accusative, as you have mentioned. According to the view of another, it is in the genitive position through an implied preposition. The Arabs hardly say "I left so-and-so that he goes," inserting "an" into the sentence; rather they say "I left him going." The "an" was inserted here only because the sentence is complete with His words ﴿that they be left alone﴾, since its meaning is: Do people think that they will be left alone, and they will not be tested, because they say, "We believe"? So His words ﴿that they be left alone﴾ are complete by their connection to "the people" without needing a further predicate. And if you make "an" in His words ﴿that they say﴾ accusative by implying a repetition of "ahasiba" (thought), it is permissible, and the meaning of the sentence becomes: Do people think that they will be left alone? Have they thought that they will say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 3:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did test those before them, so Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars﴾ (29:3)

His saying, exalted is He, means: We tested those among the nations before you, to whom We sent Our messengers, who said what your community, O Muhammad, said, [and suffered] from their enemies, and [from] Our enabling them to harm them. [This was the case] as with Moses when We sent him to the Children of Israel, and We afflicted them through Pharaoh and his chiefs; and as with Jesus when We sent him to the Children of Israel, and We afflicted those who followed him through those who turned away from him. Likewise, We afflicted your followers through your opponents among your enemies. ﴿So Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful﴾ among them in their statement "We have believed," ﴿and will surely make evident the liars﴾ among them in their statement that. Allah knows this about them before the test, during the test, and after the test. But the meaning is: Allah will manifest the truthfulness of the truthful among them in his saying "We have believed in Allah," and the lying of the liar among them, by testing them with their enemy, so that those close to them may know the truthful from the liar, in the manner we have already explained earlier.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a group of Muslims whom the polytheists tormented; some of them were tested, and some of them endured their harm until Allah brought them relief from Him.

Narration supporting this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I heard Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr say: this verse, [beginning] "Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think they will be left alone because they say, 'We believe,' and they will not be tested?..." down to His saying, "and He will surely make evident the liars," was revealed concerning Ammar ibn Yasir, when he was being tortured for the sake of Allah.

Others said: Rather, this was revealed concerning a group who had professed Islam in Makkah and remained behind from the migration. The trial by which these people were tested, over the statement of those people, was the migration by which they were examined.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Mutar, from al-Sha'bi, who said: It was revealed, meaning "Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think they will be left alone..." the two verses, concerning people in Makkah who had acknowledged Islam. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us? Evil is their judgment.﴾

Your Lord, exalted is His remembrance, says: Or do those who associate others with Allah, worshipping others alongside Him, think — and they are the ones meant by His saying ﴿those who commit evil deeds﴾ — that they can outrun Us? That is, that they can overpower Us and escape by themselves, so that We are unable to seize them and take vengeance upon them for their associating others with Allah.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

And His saying: ﴿Evil is their judgment﴾

Your Lord, exalted is His remembrance, says: Evil is their judgment which they pass, that these who commit evil deeds can outrun Us by themselves.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verses 5–6:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then indeed the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (5). And whoever strives, he only strives for himself. Indeed, Allah is Free of need from the worlds (6).﴾

His words, mighty and majestic is He, mean: Whoever hopes in Allah on the Day of His meeting and longs for His reward, then indeed the term which Allah has appointed for the raising of His creation for recompense and punishment is coming soon. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ means: and Allah, whose meeting this hoper hopes for in order to obtain His reward, is the All-Hearing of his saying, "We believe in Allah," the All-Knowing of the truthfulness of his statement, and He has known that whoever lied in it has lied. As for His words, ﴿And whoever strives, he only strives for himself﴾, it means: whoever strives against his enemy among the polytheists, he only strives for himself, because he does that seeking reward from Allah for his striving and fleeing from punishment. So Allah has no need of his doing that, because Allah is Free of need from all His creation; to Him belong the dominion, the creation and the command.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.ﴩ

Allah, the One mentioned, says: "And those who believe in Allah and His Messenger," so their faith is sound when Allah tests them and puts them to trial, and they do not turn away from their religions because of the harm the polytheists inflict upon them. ﴿And do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾ which they committed earlier in their polytheism. ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾ means: We will surely reward them for their righteous deeds in Islam, with the best of what they used to do in the state of their polytheism, along with Our removal of the evil of their deeds.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents; but if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do﴾ [29:8].

He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man﴾ in what We revealed to Our Messenger ﴿to his parents﴾ that he should act toward them with ﴿goodness﴾.

The scholars of Arabic differed over the grammatical basis for the accusative case of "ḥusnan" (goodness). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: it is put in the accusative on the presumption of repeating "waṣṣainā" (We enjoined). The meaning of the sentence, in their view, is: "And We enjoined man concerning his parents, and We enjoined him goodness." They said: a man may say "wassaituhu khayran" (I enjoined him good), meaning "with good."

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: the meaning is: "And We enjoined man that he act with goodness (ḥusn)," but the Arabs drop part of a sentence when what remains indicates what was dropped, and they make what remains operate as the dropped element would have operated. Thus "ḥusnan" is put in the accusative, even though the meaning is what you described: "We enjoined," because it has taken the place of the dropped element. He recited in support of this:

"I marvel at Dahmāʾ when they complain to us, and at Abū Dahmāʾ when he enjoins us,
goodness regarding her, as if we had been unkind to her."[[These are three verses in the mashṭūr meter of al-Sarīʿ, and they are among the evidences cited by al-Farrāʾ in his Maʿānī al-Qurʾān (p. 178). He said: The Arabs say "uwṣīka bihi khayran" (I enjoin you regarding him, good) and "āmuruka bihi khayran" (I command you regarding him, good), and its meaning is: "I command you that you act toward him," then "an" is dropped, so the good is attached to the enjoining and the commanding. The poet said: "I marvel..." and the verses.]]

He said: the meaning of His saying "yūṣīnā khayran" is: that we act toward her with goodness; he was content with "yūṣīnā" as an indication of it. He said: this is like His saying: ﴿so he began passing his hand﴾, meaning "he began passing his hand over them."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾

He says: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man﴾, and We said to him: if your parents strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, that it is not that I have a partner, then do not obey them, so that you would associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, seeking their pleasure; rather, oppose them in that. ﴿To Me is your return﴾: He, exalted is His mention, says: to Me is your resort and your destination on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And I will inform you about what you used to do﴾: He says: I will inform you of what you used to do in the world of righteous deeds and their evil, then I will recompense you for them: the good-doer with goodness, and the evil-doer with what he deserves.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.

Those who said so:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, regarding ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents...﴾ up to His saying ﴿and I will inform you about what you used to do﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ when he emigrated; his mother said: "By Allah, I will not be shaded by a roof until you return." So Allah revealed concerning that that he should be good to them both, and not obey them in polytheism.

**The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾ (9)**

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those who believe﴾ in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ from among the actions. That means they perform the obligations of Allah and avoid His prohibitions. ﴿We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾ into the entrance of the righteous, which is Paradise.

* *

**The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah," but when they are harmed for the sake of Allah, they consider the trial of people as the punishment of Allah. And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾ (10)**

He, the Exalted, says: And among the people are those who say, "We affirmed Allah, so we declared Him one." But when the polytheists harm them for their affirmation of Allah, they regard the people's persecution of them in this world as equal to the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter, so they apostatize from their faith in Allah, returning to disbelief in Him. ﴿And if victory comes from your Lord﴾, O Muhammad, to the people of faith in Him, ﴿they will surely say﴾, these apostates from their faith, who regard the people's trial as the punishment of Allah: ﴿Indeed, we were﴾, O believers, ﴿with you﴾, supporting you against your enemies, falsely and deceptively. Allah says: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing﴾, O people, of everyone ﴿of what is within the breasts of the worlds﴾, all His creation, both those who say "We believe in Allah" and others? So when one is harmed for Allah, he apostatizes from the religion of Allah. How then could one deceive the One to whom nothing is hidden, and from whom no secret or public matter is concealed?

It is in accordance with what we have said regarding this that the people of ta'wil (interpretation) have spoken.

*Mention of those who said that:*

It was related to me by Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: My father related to me, who said: My paternal uncle related to me, who said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah," but when they are harmed for the sake of Allah, they consider the trial of people as the punishment of Allah﴾. He said: Their trial is that one apostatizes from the religion of Allah when he is harmed for Allah.

It was related to me by Muhammad ibn 'Amr, who said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, who said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿So when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he considers the trial of people as the punishment of Allah...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and Allah will surely make evident the hypocrites﴾. He said: They are people who believe with their tongues. When a affliction from Allah or a calamity befalls them in themselves, they are tried, and they regard that in this world as the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter.

It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah..."﴾ the verse: It was revealed concerning some hypocrites in Mecca who used to believe, but when they were harmed and afflicted with calamity from the polytheists, they returned to disbelief out of fear of those who harmed them, and they regarded the harm of people in this world as the punishment of Allah.

It was related to me by Yunus, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿So when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he considers the trial of people as the punishment of Allah﴾: He is the hypocrite who, when harmed for Allah, turns away from the religion and disbelieves, and regards the trial of people as the punishment of Allah.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a group of people of faith in Mecca who went out as emigrants, but they were overtaken and seized, and when the harm they suffered reached them, they gave the polytheists what they wanted from them.

The polytheists brought them out with them on the day of Badr, and some of them were struck and some were killed. The Muslims said: These companions of ours were Muslims, but they were coerced. So they asked forgiveness for them, and it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, [the angels] say, "In what were you engaged?"...﴾ up to the end of the verse. Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us. *Then I said: "Call, and I will call, for more resounding is the voice that two callers call."*

He means: "Call, and let me call," and its meaning is: "If you call, I will call."

* *

And His saying: ﴿"But they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars"﴾

This is Allah's refutation of the polytheists who said to those who believed ﴿"Follow our way and we will bear your sins"﴾. The verse of the poem, as cited in the footnote of the editor: The line is attributed to Dathar ibn Shaybān al-Namri (Lisan al-Arab: nada). It is said: "So-and-so has a more resonant voice than so-and-so," meaning: more far-reaching in his course and louder in voice. Al-Asma'i recited for Dathar ibn Shaybān al-Namri: *My beloved said, when we were afflicted: "The sons of al-Qarm al-Hijan will overtake us."* *Then I said: "Call, and I will call, for more resounding is the voice that two callers call."* In Fara'id al-Qala'id, which is al-Ayni's small commentary on the shawahid, in the chapter on the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of the verb, it is said that the line was composed by al-A'sha or al-Huṭay'a, according to what Ibn Ya'ish claimed, or Rabi'a, a Hashm, according to what al-Zamakhshari claimed, or Dathar ibn Shaybān al-Namri, according to what Ibn Burri claimed. The author has transmitted it in full.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 13–14:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they will surely carry their own burdens, and [other] burdens along with their burdens. And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent.﴾ [29:13]

The Exalted says: Those polytheists who said to the believers, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins," will surely carry their own burdens, that is, their own sins and their misdeeds, and the burdens of those whom they led astray and turned away from the way of God, along with their own burdens. And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to falsely claim in this world, by their promising them falsehoods and by their saying to them, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins," so they fabricated lies in this regard.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And they will surely carry their burdens﴾, meaning their sins, ﴿and [other] burdens along with their burdens﴾, he said: the sins of those whom they led astray.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And they will surely carry their burdens and [other] burdens along with their burdens﴾. And he recited His saying: ﴿That they may bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is what they bear.﴾ [16:25] He said: This is His saying: ﴿and [other] burdens along with their burdens﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years. Then the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.﴾ [29:14]

This is a warning from God, the Exalted, to these polytheists of Quraysh, who said to the believers, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins." He says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not let what you and your companions encounter of harm from these polytheists grieve you, O Muhammad. For although I give them respite and prolong their reprieve, the end of their affair is destruction, while the end of your affair and that of your companions is elevation and victory over them, and deliverance from the punishment that will befall them. This is as We did with Noah when We sent him to his people; he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, calling them to monotheism and to abandoning the gods and idols. Yet his calling them to God did not increase them in anything but flight, rather than turning toward Him and accepting the counsel from God that he brought them.

It is mentioned that he was sent to his people when he was three hundred and fifty years old.

As follows:

Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us, saying: Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, saying: Awn ibn Abi Shaddad narrated to us, saying: God sent Noah to his people when he was three hundred and fifty years old. He remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, then he lived after that three hundred and fifty years. Then the flood seized them, meaning God, the Exalted, says: He destroyed them with abundant water. Every abundant water that spreads and overflows is called a "tufan" by the Arabs, whether it is a torrent or otherwise, and likewise death, when it is widespread and abundant, is also called "tufan" by them. From this is the saying of the rajiz (rajaz poet):

"The tufan of deadly, sweeping death destroyed them"

[This verse is from the half-line meter of rajaz and is among the evidences cited by Abu Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 184a), who said: "Tufan" metaphorically means any overflowing, spreading water, whether from a torrent or otherwise, and likewise death when it is sweeping and widespread and abundant. He said: "The tufan destroyed them..." the verse. The author quoted it verbatim. In (Lisan al-Arab: t-w-f): "al-tufan" is water that covers every place. It was also said: "tufan" is anything from everything that is abundant and encompassing all the group, like a drowning that covers many cities, a devastating slaughter, and a sweeping death, which is called tufan. All of this was used to explain His saying, "Then the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers."]

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿Then the flood seized them﴾, he said: It is the water that was sent upon them.

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: "al-Tufan" is the drowning.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿while they were wrongdoers﴾

He means: while they were wronging themselves through their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 15:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the Ark, and made it a sign for the worlds.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: So We saved Noah and the companions of his ship, namely those whom He carried in his ship from among his offspring and their wives.

We have already explained this earlier, and mentioned the reports concerning it, so that is sufficient and there is no need to repeat it in this place.

﴿And made it a sign for the worlds⦆ means: and We made the ship in which We saved him and his companions a lesson and an admonition for the worlds, and a proof against them.

Interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the Ark...﴾ the verse. He said: God preserved it as a sign for the people at the top of al-Judi.

If it were said that the meaning of ﴿And made it a sign for the worlds⦆ is: And We made Our punishment of them a sign for the worlds, and that the pronoun in His words ﴿and made it⦆ refers to the punishment or the wrath or the like, since that had already been mentioned in His words ﴿So the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾, that would be a valid line of interpretation.

It is said: He did so in this manner because the report about the matter of Noah and Abraham and their peoples, and all others whom Allah mentioned among the messengers and communities in this surah and elsewhere, is only a reminder from Allah, exalted is His remembrance, to those whose mention He begins with before the digression of the report, and a warning from Him to them that what befell them may befall them. So it is as if it were said at this point: "So worship Him, and be grateful to Him; to Him you will be returned. Then you, the people of Quraysh, denied your messenger Muhammad, just as those denied Abraham." Then He put in place of "then you denied" the words "And if you deny, then communities before you have denied," since that indicates the report of their denial of their messenger. Then He returned to the report about Abraham and his people, and completed his story and theirs with His saying: ﴿So there was not the answer of his people﴾.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Kill him or burn him," but Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ (24)

Allah, the Exalted, says: The answer of Abraham's people to him, when he said to them, ﴿Worship Allah and fear Him; that is better for you, if you only knew,﴾ was nothing but that some of them said to others, ﴿"Kill him or burn him,"﴾ with fire. So they did it: they intended to burn him with fire, kindled a fire for him, and threw him into it. Then Allah saved him from it, and did not give it power over him; rather, He made it cool and safe for him.

As related to us:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿So the answer of [his people] was only that they said, "Kill him or burn him," but Allah saved him from the fire﴾: He said, "Ka'b said: 'Nothing was burned of him except his bonds.'" ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾: Allah, the Exalted, says: Indeed, in Our saving Abraham from the fire, into which he was cast while it was blazing, and in Our making it cool and safe for him, are proofs and arguments for a people who affirm the proofs and arguments when they witness and see them.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 29, verse 25:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And he said, "You have only taken, instead of Allah, idols out of affection among yourselves in the life of this world. Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny others and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers."﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, relating the words of Ibrahim to his people: ﴿And he said﴾ — Ibrahim to his people: O my people, ﴿you have only taken, instead of Allah, idols﴾.

The reciters differed over the recitation of His words ﴿mawadata baynikum﴾. The majority of the reciters of Madina and Syria, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿mawaddatan﴾ with "mawadda" in the accusative and without an annexation, with ﴿baynakum﴾ in the accusative. Some of the Kufans recited ﴿mawaddata baynikum﴾ with "al-mawadda" in the accusative and annexed to ﴿baynikum﴾, with ﴿baynikum﴾ in the genitive. Those who recited ﴿mawaddatan﴾ in the accusative apparently directed the meaning of the statement to: ﴿innama ittakhadhtum﴾ (you have only taken), O people, ﴿idols, a affection among yourselves﴾. They made "innama" a single particle and placed the verb ﴿ittakhadhtum﴾ upon the idols, putting them in the accusative with the meaning: you have taken them as an affection among yourselves, loving one another in worshipping them and mutually befriending one another in serving them, so that you connect through them. Some reciters of Makka and Basra recited ﴿mawaddatu baynikum﴾ with "mawadda" in the nominative and annexed to "al-bayn", with "al-bayn" in the genitive. Those who recited it thus made "inna ma" two particles, with the sense: indeed, those you have taken instead of Allah as idols are only your affection for the world, so they put "mawadda" in the nominative as the predicate of "inna". It is also permissible that, in their recitation, they put it in the nominative governed by "innama" as a single particle, with the statement ending at ﴿innama ittakhadhtum min duni Allahi awthanan﴾, and then the statement begins anew, saying: your affection for those idols will not benefit you; it is only an affection among you in your life in this world, and then it is cut off. When this meaning is intended, "mawadda" is in the nominative as a qualifier by His words ﴿fi al-hayat al-dunya﴾. It is also permissible that they intended to raise "mawadda" by making it nominative as the pronoun "hiya" (it).

These three readings are close in meaning, because those who took the idols as gods to worship, took them as an affection among themselves, and they had an affection in the life of this world, and then it is cut off from them. Whichever of these a reciter recites is correct, due to the closeness of their meanings and the fame of each of these readings among the reciters of the regions.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) said what we have said in this regard.

Mention of those who said that:

Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny others and curse one another"﴾, he said: every friendship in the world becomes enmity for its people on the Day of Resurrection, except the friendship of the righteous.

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Then on the Day of Resurrection, O you who showed affection to one another in worshipping idols and statues, and who connected with one another in serving them, when you arrive before your Lord and witness what Allah has prepared for you because of the connection and affection you had in the world, of painful punishment, ﴿some of you will deny others﴾ — he says: some of you will disown others, and some of you will curse others.

His saying, may His majesty be praised: The final destination of all of you, O worshippers of idols and what you worship, is the Fire. ﴿And you will have no helpers﴾ — he says: and you, O people who took gods instead of Allah, have no helpers from Allah who will support you when He casts you into the Fire of Hell, to rescue you from His punishment.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:** ﴿And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and We placed in his offspring prophethood and the Book, and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous.﴾ (29:27)

As narrated:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob﴾ he said: "They are the two sons of Abraham."

Mention of those who said this:

Scholars of ta'wil (interpretation) have said what we have said on this matter.

Others said: Rather, it was that they used to pelt those who passed by them.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: 'Umar ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Ikrimah say regarding His words: ﴿and commit the evil in your gatherings﴾: "They used to harm the people of the road, pelting those who passed by them."

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿and commit the evil in your gatherings﴾, he said: "They used to commit the abomination in their gatherings."

'Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿and commit the evil in your gatherings﴾, he said: "In your assemblies."

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Abraham said to the angels, the messengers, when they said to him: ﴿Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this town, for its people have been wrongdoers.﴾ They did not make an exception among them, since they described them as wrongdoers. ﴿Indeed, Lut is there,﴾ and he is not among the wrongdoers; rather, he is a messenger of Allah, and one of the people of faith in Him and obedience to Him. So the messengers said to him: ﴿We are most knowing of who is in it,﴾ of the wrongdoers who disbelieve in Allah more than you do. * *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But when Our messengers came to Lut, he was distressed on their account and felt powerless to protect them, and they said, "Do not fear, nor grieve. The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. So he said, "O my people, worship Allah and expect the Last Day and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption."﴾ (36)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: The people of Madyan denied Shu'ayb in what he brought them from Allah of the message, so the quake of punishment seized them. ﴿"And they became in their homes prostrate"﴾ — jathiman (prostrate, fallen), some of them upon others, dead.

He, the Exalted, says: The likeness of those who take as protectors the gods and idols other than Allah, hoping for their help and benefit when they are in need of them, is (a likeness) of their weakness in devising, the baseness of their reasoning, and the poor choice they make for themselves. ﴿Like the spider⦆ in its weakness and its lack of devising for itself, ﴿which makes for itself a house⦆ so that it may shelter itself, but it avails it nothing when it is in need of it. Likewise, these polytheists: their protectors whom they took besides Allah, as something (of worth), do not avail them when the affair of Allah befalls them and His wrath descends upon them, nor do they repel from them what Allah has brought down of His wrath through their worshipping them.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿The likeness of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider⦆, he said: This is a likeness which Allah has struck for the polytheist: the likeness of his god whom he calls upon besides Allah is like the spider's house, frail and weak, which benefits him not.

The readers differed over the recitation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows what you call upon﴾. The majority of the readers of the principal cities recited ﴿tad'una﴾ (تَدْعُونَ) with the letter ta' (تاء), meaning an address to the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾ — O people — ﴿knows what you call upon besides Him of anything﴾. Abu 'Amr recited it ﴿yad'una﴾ (يَدْعُونَ) with the letter ya' (ياء), meaning a report about the nations: that Allah knows what those whom We destroyed from the nations call upon, ﴿besides Him of anything﴾.

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is the recitation of the one who recites with the ta'. This is because, if it were a report about the nations whom Allah mentioned that He destroyed, the statement would be: "Indeed, Allah knows what they used to call upon," since the people, at the time this report was revealed to the Prophet of Allah, were no longer present, having been destroyed and perished. It is only said: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows what you call upon﴾ when the address is directed at those who are present, not at those who have perished.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 44–45:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Recite﴾, meaning: read ﴿what has been revealed to you of the Book﴾, meaning: what has been sent down to you of this Qur'an. ﴿And establish the prayer﴾, meaning: perform the prayer that Allah has prescribed for you, with its limits. ﴿Indeed, the prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of "prayer" mentioned in this place. Some of them said: it refers to the Qur'an that is recited in the place of prayer, or in the prayer.

Those who said that:

ʿAli narrated to me, he said: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, he said: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾, he says: in the prayer there is a restraint and a deterrent from the disobedience of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is: the remembrance of Allah of you is better than your remembrance of Him.

Those who said that:

Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Rabiʿa, he said: Ibn ʿAbbas said to me: Do you know what His saying means: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾? I said: Yes. He said: What is it? I said: Glorification, praise and magnification in the prayer, and reciting the Qur'an and the like. He said: You have said a strange thing, and it is not as you say. Rather, it means: the remembrance of Allah of you, when He commands or forbids you, if you remember Him, is greater than your remembrance of Him.

Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ibn Rabiʿa, from Ibn ʿAbbas, he said: The remembrance of Allah of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAta', from ʿAbd Allah ibn Rabiʿa, he said: Ibn ʿAbbas asked me about the saying of Allah: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾. I said: His remembrance with glorification, magnification and the Qur'an is good, and His remembrance at the forbidden things restrains from them. He said: You have said a wondrous thing, and it is not as you said; rather, the remembrance of Allah of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Rabiʿa, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, he said: Allah's remembrance of the servant is better than his remembrance of Him.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, Ibn al-Muthanna said: ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, and Ibn Wakiʿ said: ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Dawud narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, he said: I was sitting with Ibn ʿAbbas when a man came and asked Ibn ʿAbbas about "the remembrance of Allah is greater." Ibn ʿAbbas said: The prayer and fasting. He said: That is the remembrance of Allah. A man said: I left a man in my camp saying other than this. He said: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, Allah's remembrance of the servants is greater than the servants' remembrance of Him. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Your companion has spoken the truth, by Allah.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yaʿqub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbas and said: Tell me about the saying of Allah: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾. He said: His remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Dawud, from ʿIkrima: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, he said: Allah's remembrance of the servant is better than his remembrance of Him.

Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, he said: Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from ʿAtiyya: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, he said: it is His saying: ﴿So remember Me, I will remember you﴾, and Allah's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

ʿAli narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah﴾, toward His servants when they remember Him, ﴿is greater﴾ than your remembrance of Him.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, he said: Allah's remembrance of His servant is greater than the servant's remembrance of his Lord, in prayer or otherwise.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, from Ibn ʿAbbas, he said: Allah's remembrance of you, when you remember Him, is greater than your remembrance of Him.

Others said: it admits both meanings together, meaning the first saying we mentioned and the second.

Yaʿqub narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Khalid, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, he said: It has two aspects: the remembrance of Allah is greater than anything else, and Allah's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: the remembrance of Allah of the servant in prayer is greater than the prayer.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: and the prayer you perform, and Allah's remembrance of you in it, is greater than what the prayer has forbidden you of immorality and wrongdoing.

Abu Ja'far said: The sayings most resembling what the apparent wording of the revelation indicates are the saying of one who said: "And Allah's remembrance of you is better than your remembrance of Him."

He says: And Allah knows what you do, O people, in your prayers, of establishing its limits or neglecting that and your other affairs, and He will recompense you for that. He says: so beware of wasting any of its limits. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: ʿUmar ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, from al-ʿUyzar ibn Huraith, from a man, from Salman, that he was asked: Which deed is best? He said: Do you not read the Qur'an: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾? Nothing is better than the remembrance of Allah.

Ibn Humayd Ahmad ibn al-Mughira al-Himsi narrated to us, he said: ʿAli ibn ʿAyyash narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, he said: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from Rabi'a ibn Yazid, from Isma'il ibn ʿUbayd Allah, from Umm al-Darda', that she said: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾. If you pray, it is from the remembrance of Allah; if you fast, it is from the remembrance of Allah; every good you do is from the remembrance of Allah, and every evil you avoid is from the remembrance of Allah; and the best of that is glorifying Allah.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, he said: Nothing is greater than the remembrance of Allah. He said: It is the greatest of all things, and he recited: ﴿Establish the prayer for My remembrance﴾, he said: for the remembrance of Allah; and He did not describe it at the time of fighting except as greater.

Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Ishaq, he said: A man said to Salman: Which deed is best? He said: The remembrance of Allah.

Others said: it admits both meanings together, meaning the first saying we mentioned and the second.

Those who said that:

Yaʿqub narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Khalid, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, he said: It has two aspects: the remembrance of Allah is greater than anything else, and Allah's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Khalid al-Hadhdha' narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, he said: It has two aspects: Allah's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him, and the remembrance of Allah at what is forbidden.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: the remembrance of Allah of the servant in prayer is greater than the prayer.

Those who said that:

Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, he said: ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, from Israʾil, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik regarding His saying: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, he said: Allah's remembrance of the servant in prayer is greater than the prayer.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: and the prayer you perform, and Allah's remembrance of you in it, is greater than what the prayer has forbidden you of immorality and wrongdoing.

Ahmad ibn al-Mughira al-Himsi narrated to me, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-ʿAttar narrated to us, he said: Artat narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, the prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾: and the state you are in of Allah's remembrance is greater.

Abu Ja'far said: The sayings most resembling what the apparent wording of the revelation indicates are the saying of one who said: "And Allah's remembrance of you is better than your remembrance of Him."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And Allah knows what you do﴾

He says: And Allah knows what you do, O people, in your prayers, of establishing its limits or neglecting that and your other affairs, and He will recompense you for that. He says: so beware of wasting any of its limits. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 46:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a manner that is best, except for those of them who have wronged, and say: "We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you. And our God and your God is one, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."﴾ (29:46)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And do not argue﴾, O believers in God and His Messenger, ﴿with the People of the Book [the Jews and the Christians] except in a manner that is best﴾, meaning: except with what is good of speech, which is calling to God by His signs and drawing attention to His proofs.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except for those of them who have wronged﴾

The exegetes differed concerning its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: except for those who refused to acknowledge to you the payment of the jizyah (poll tax) and took up war against you instead of that. They are wrongdoers, so argue with them by the sword until they become Muslim or pay the jizyah.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a manner that is best, except for those of them who have wronged﴾, he said: "Those who fight and do not give the jizyah."

Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "Those who fight you and do not give you the jizyah."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a manner that is best﴾, he said: "If they say something evil, say something good." ﴿except for those of them who have wronged﴾: "Take retribution against them."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿except for those of them who have wronged﴾, he said: "They said: 'With God there is a god,' or 'He has a son,' or 'He has a partner,' or 'the hand of God is shackled,' or 'God is poor,' or 'they harmed Muhammad ﷺ.' He said: 'They are the People of the Book.'"

Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Salim, from Sa'id: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a manner that is best, except for those of them who have wronged﴾, he said: "The people of war; whoever has no covenant, argue with him by the sword."

Others said: the meaning of that is: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book﴾ who have believed in it and followed its Messenger concerning what they have told you of what is in their books ﴿except in a manner that is best, except for those of them who have wronged﴾ by persisting in their disbelief. And they said: this verse is muhkam (definitive) and not abrogated.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a manner that is best﴾: "It is not abrogated. One should not argue with those of them who have believed, since perhaps they may say something good concerning the Book of God which you do not know, so do not argue with it. And one should argue only with those who have wronged, namely those of them who persist in their religion." He said: "It is the one who is argued with, and it is said to him, 'with the sword'" [[i.e., the sword is raised against him. In Lisan al-Arab (under q-w-l) it is said: the Arabs use "qala" as an expression for all actions, applying it to other than speech and the tongue; so they say "qala bi-yadihi," meaning he took; "qala bi-rijlihi," meaning he walked. A poet said: "And the two eyes said to him: hearing and obedience," meaning they gestured. "Qala bi-thawbihi" means he raised it. All of this is figurative and extended usage. In the original text: "wa-yuqal lahu: al-sabt" is a scribal distortion.]]. He said: "These are Jews. He said: 'No Christians were in the abode of the Hijrah; rather, the Jews were the ones who spoke with and made alliances with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the Nadir betrayed on the day of Uhud, and Qurayza betrayed on the day of the Confederates.'"

Others said: rather, this verse was revealed before the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to fight, and they said: it is abrogated, abrogated by His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a manner that is best," then it was abrogated after that; He commanded fighting them in Surat Bara'ah, and there is no argument more severe than the sword, until they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God ﷺ, or they acknowledge the kharaj (tribute).

The most correct of these opinions is the view of those who said: by His saying: ﴿except for those of them who have wronged﴾ is meant: except for those who refused to pay the jizyah and took up war in place of it.

If someone says: is there any wrongdoer among the People of the Book except one who does not pay the jizyah? It is said: all of them, though they are wrongdoers to themselves through their disbelief in God and their denial of His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, yet He did not mean by His saying: ﴿except for those of them who have wronged﴾ the wrong done to themselves. Rather He meant: except for those of them who have wronged the people of faith in God and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ; those are the ones to argue with by fighting.

We have said that this is the most correct of the opinions concerning it because God, may His remembrance be exalted, permitted the believers to argue with the wrongdoers among the People of the Book in other than the best manner, by His saying: ﴿except for those of them who have wronged﴾. It is known, since He permitted them to argue with them, that those for whom they were not permitted to argue except in the best manner are other than those for whom He permitted that, and that they are not the believer among them; for it is not permissible to argue with a believer among them except in what is not the truth, because if he comes with what is not the truth, he has become in the sense of the wrongdoers in that wherein he opposed the truth. Since this is so, it becomes clear that there is no meaning to the view of those who said: by His saying: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book﴾ is meant the believers among them. Likewise there is no meaning to the view of those who said: this verse was revealed before the command to fight, and claimed it is abrogated; for there is no report that settles the matter on this, nor any indication of its soundness from natural reason.

We have explained in more than one place in our book that it is not permissible to rule that a judgment of God in His Book is abrogated except by a proof that must be accepted, whether from a report or from reason.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And say: "We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you. And our God and your God is one, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted, to the believers in Him and His Messenger, whom He forbade from arguing with the People of the Book except in the best manner: when the People of the Book tell you, O people, about their books, and inform you of them with what could and might be true or false, and you do not know their state and situation in that, then say to them: ﴿"We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you"﴾ from the Torah and the Gospel. ("And our God and your God is one") meaning: our worshipped one and your worshipped one is one. ﴿"And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him"﴾, meaning: we are humbly submissive to Him in obedience in what He commands us and forbids us.

The report from the Messenger of God ﷺ has come in accordance with what we have said concerning this.

Mention of the narration to that effect:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Ali informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the people of Islam. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Do not believe the People of the Book, nor disbelieve them, but say: ﴿'We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you, and our God and your God is one, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.'﴾"

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: Some Jews used to tell some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Do not believe them, nor disbelieve them; ﴿say: 'We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you.'﴾"

He said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Sulayman, from 'Umarah ibn 'Umayr, from Hurayth ibn Zuhayr, from Abdullah, who said: Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for they will not guide you, and they have gone astray; either you will deny a truth or affirm a falsehood. For there is no one among the People of the Book except that in his heart there is a "taliyah" calling him to his religion, like the "taliyat al-mal" [[Taliyah is the active participle of talaahu, yatluhu: meaning he followed him. It intends: a follower calling him to hold fast to his religion. "Taliyat al-mal" may mean: the young camel that follows its mothers among the young of camels and the like.]].

Mujahid used to say concerning that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated this to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿except for those of them who have wronged﴾, he said: "They said: 'With God there is a god,' or 'He has a son,' or 'He has a partner,' or 'the hand of God is shackled,' or 'God is poor,' or 'they harmed Muhammad.'" ﴿And say: "We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you"﴾ to those among the People of the Book who do not say this.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 47–48:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And thus We have sent down to you the Book. Those to whom We gave the Book believe in it, and among these there are those who believe in it. And none deny Our signs except the disbelievers.﴾ (47)

The Exalted says: Just as We sent down Books to the messengers before you, O Muhammad, ﴿thus We have sent down to you﴾ this ﴿Book. Those to whom We gave the Book﴾ before you, from the Children of Israel, ﴿believe in it. And among these there are those who believe in it.﴾ He says: and among those who are now present with you, there are those who believe in it, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, and those among the Children of Israel who believed in His Messenger.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And none deny Our signs except the disbelievers﴾

The Exalted says: None deny Our proofs and evidences except the one who denies Our blessings upon him and rejects Our Oneness and Lordship knowingly, out of obstinacy toward Us.

As narrated:

⁕ Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa‛id told us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And none deny Our signs except the disbelievers﴾: He said: denial only occurs after knowledge.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And you did not recite any Book before it, nor did you write it with your right hand; otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubt.﴾ (48)

The Exalted says: ﴿And you were not﴾ O Muhammad ﴿reciting﴾, meaning: reading ﴿before it﴾, meaning: before this Book which We have sent down to you, ﴿any book, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾. He says: you did not write with your right hand, but you were unlettered. ﴿Otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾. He says: had you, before the revelation came to you, been reading a Book or writing it with your right hand, ﴿then the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾. He says: then they would have doubted, because of that, your matter and what you brought them from your Lord of this Book which you recite to them, — the falsifiers who say that it is rhymed prose and soothsaying, and that it is the fables of the ancients.

Those of the interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said regarding that.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa‛d told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And you did not recite any Book before it, nor did you write it with your right hand; otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾: He said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was unlettered; he did not read anything nor write.

⁕ Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa‛id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And you did not recite any Book before it, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾: He said: The Prophet of Allah did not read any book before it, nor write it with his right hand. He said: he was unlettered, and the unlettered is one who does not write.

⁕ Ibn Wakiʿ told us, saying: Abu Usamah told us, from Idris al-Awdi, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And you did not recite any Book before it, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾: He said: The People of the Book used to find in their books that the Prophet (ﷺ) would not write with his right hand nor read a book, so this verse was revealed.

And we have also said similarly regarding His saying: ﴿otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾, they said:

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa‛id told us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾: Otherwise they would have said: this is only something Muhammad (ﷺ) learned and wrote down.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us; all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the word of God: ﴿otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾: He said: Quraysh.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 49:

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge. And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers.﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of His words, ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge.﴾ Some of them said: it refers to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: the meaning of the statement is: rather, the presence of [the description of] Muhammad (ﷺ) in their books, that he cannot write nor read, and that he is unlettered (ummi), are clear signs in their breasts.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾: He said: Allah the Exalted had revealed concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) in the Torah and the Gospel to the people of knowledge, and taught it to them, and made it a sign for them, and said to them: the sign of his prophethood is that he will emerge, when he emerges, not knowing any book, and not writing it with his right hand. These are the clear signs.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words, ﴿And you did not recite before it any book﴾: He said: the Prophet of Allah did not write nor read, and likewise Allah made his description in the Torah and the Gospel, that he is an unlettered prophet who neither reads nor writes, and this is the clear sign in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾: [they are] from the People of the Book, who affirmed Muhammad, his description and his prophethood.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, ﴿Rather, it is clear signs﴾: He said: Allah revealed the matter of Muhammad in the Torah and the Gospel to the people of knowledge; rather, he is a clear sign in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge, meaning: the Prophet (ﷺ).

Others said: it refers to the Qur'an, and they said: the meaning of the statement is: rather, this Qur'an is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge, from among the believers in Muhammad (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His words, ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾: The Qur'an is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge, meaning the believers.

The more correct of the two opinions regarding this, in my view, is the opinion of the one who said: it refers to: rather, the knowledge that you did not recite any book before this one, nor write it with your right hand, [is] clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge from the People of the Book.

I only said this is the more appropriate of the two interpretations of the verse because His words, ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾, lie between two reports from Allah about His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), so it being a report about him is more fitting than it being a report about the Book, whose report had already ended before.

* *

And His words: ﴿And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: none deny the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his proofs, and reject the knowledge that is known from the books of Allah, which He sent down to His prophets, concerning the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), his prophethood and his mission, except the wrongdoers, meaning those who wronged themselves by their disbelief in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "Why has not a sign been sent down upon him from his Lord?" Say, "Signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."﴾

His exalted remembrance says: The polytheists of Quraysh said, "Why has a sign not been sent down upon Muhammad from his Lord, one that would be a proof of Allah against us, just as the she-camel was made a sign for Salih, and the table spread (al-ma'idah) was a sign for Jesus?" Say, O Muhammad: "Signs are only with Allah; none is able to bring them except Him." ﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾: I am only a warner to you, warning you of the punishment and retribution of Allah for your disbelief in His Messenger, and in what has come to you from your Lord. ﴿Clear﴾ means: he has made his warning clear to you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verses 51–52:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book being recited to them? Indeed in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.﴾ (29:51)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Is it not sufficient for these polytheists, O Muhammad, who say: "Why was a sign not sent down to Muhammad from his Lord," any of the signs and proofs? ﴿That We have sent down to you this Book﴾ — this — ﴿being recited to them﴾ — meaning, being read to them. ﴿Indeed in that is mercy﴾ — meaning: indeed in this Book which We have sent down to them is mercy for those who believe in it, and a reminder by which they are reminded through the lesson and admonition contained in it.

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed because some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ copied out some of the books of the People of the Book.

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Yahya ibn Ja'da, that some Muslims came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ with books in which they had written some of what the Jews say. When he looked at them he threw them away, then said: "Enough folly for a people — or misguidance for a people — that they turn away from what their prophet has brought them to what another prophet has brought, or to another people." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book being recited to them? Indeed in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.﴾

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth. And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah — it is they who are the losers.﴾ (29:52)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you: "Why was a sign not sent down to you from your Lord," and to those among your people who deny Our signs: Allah is sufficient, O people, as a witness between me and you, a witness for me and against you; for He knows the one of us who is in the right from the one who is in the wrong, and He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, nothing in them being hidden from Him. He is the one who will recompense each party of us according to what it deserves: the one in the right for his steadfastness upon the truth, and the one in the wrong for his falsehood according to what he deserves. ﴿And those who believe in falsehood﴾ — meaning: they affirm polytheism, they acknowledge it, and disbelieve in Allah — meaning: they deny Allah ﴿it is they who are the losers﴾ — meaning: they are the ones who are defrauded in their bargain.

In the same sense as what we have said concerning His saying ﴿and those who believe in falsehood﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and those who believe in falsehood﴾: it is shirk (associating partners with Allah).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verses 53–54:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them. And it will surely come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive﴾ [29:53].

He, may He be exalted, says: These people who say it from your people, O Muhammad, are asking you to hasten the punishment, saying: "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord with the punishment?" And they say: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾ [8:32]. Were it not for a term that I have specified for them, so that I would not destroy them until they complete and reach it, the punishment would have come upon them quickly.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And it will surely come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive﴾.

He says: The punishment will surely come upon them suddenly, while they do not know the time of its arrival before it arrives.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment﴾, he said: Some ignorant people of this ummah said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment﴾ — the verse.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾ [29:54].

He, may He be exalted, says: These polytheists ask you, O Muhammad, to hasten the coming of the punishment and its descent upon them, while Hell encompasses them; nothing remains but that they enter it. And it was said: that refers to the sea.

Mention of those who said that:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 55–56:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day the punishment will envelop them from above them and from beneath their feet, and He will say: "Taste what you used to do."﴾

Exalted is His remembrance says: ﴿And indeed, Hell will surely encompass the disbelievers﴾ on the Day the punishment envelops the disbelievers, from above them in Hell, and from beneath their feet.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿On the Day the punishment will envelop them from above them and from beneath their feet﴾: that is, in the Fire.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He will say: "Taste what you used to do."﴾

Exalted is His remembrance says: And Allah will say to them: "Taste what you used to do in the world of acts of disobedience to Allah and what displeases Him therein." Regarding ﴿And He will say (wayaqulu)﴾ with the yā' (ya), the majority of the readers of the principal cities recited it so, except Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Amr, for they recited it with the nūn: ﴿And We will say (wanaqulu)﴾. The reading that is correct in our view is with the yā', due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone.﴾

Exalted is His remembrance says to the believers among His servants who affirmed His oneness and believed in Me and in My Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, My earth is vast﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning intended by the report about the vastness of the earth. Some of them said: what is meant by this is that it has not become too narrow for you so that you remain in a place of it where it is not lawful for you to dwell; rather, if disobedience to Allah is practised in a place of it and you are unable to change it, then flee from it.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, My earth is vast﴾: He said: When disobedience is practised in it, leave it.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, My earth is vast﴾, he said: When disobedience is practised in it, leave it.

* Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Laith, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Flee, for indeed My earth is vast.

* Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sharik, from Mansur, from 'Ata', who said: When you are commanded to acts of disobedience, flee, for indeed My earth is vast.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Mansur, from 'Ata', regarding ﴿Indeed, My earth is vast﴾, he said: Keeping away from the people of disobedience.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, My earth is vast﴾, so emigrate and strive.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone﴾. I said: He means by this those believers who were in Mecca. He said: Yes.

Others said: the meaning of that is: that what is brought forth from My earth for you of provision is vast for you.

Those who said that:

* al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to me, from Shaddad ibn Sa'id ibn Malik Abu Talhah al-Rasibi, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir al-Mi'wali, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir al-'Amiri, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, My earth is vast﴾: he said: Indeed My provision for you is vast.

* Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, from Shaddad, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, from Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir: ﴿Indeed, My earth is vast﴾, he said: My provision for you is vast.

The more preferable of the two opinions regarding the interpretation of the verse is the view of those who said: the meaning is that Indeed My earth is vast, so flee from those who prevent you from acting in obedience to Me; this is indicated by His saying: ﴿so worship Me alone﴾, and because that is the more apparent of its two meanings. For when He describes the earth as vast, the usual sense of describing it so is that it is not entirely constricted for one whose particular place has become constricted for him, and not that He describes it with abundance of goodness and fertility.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿so worship Me alone﴾

It means: devote your worship and obedience to Me sincerely, and do not obey any of My creation in disobedience to Me.
