Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verses 57–59:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned.﴾ ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds – We will surely settle them in lofty chambers in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. How excellent is the reward of the workers,﴾ ﴿those who were patient and upon their Lord they rely.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers in Him among the companions of His Prophet: Emigrate from the land of polytheism, from Makkah to the land of Islam, Madinah, for My earth is spacious. So be patient in worshipping Me, and devote your obedience to Me, for you are all going to die and will return to Me, since every living soul tastes death, and then after death you will be returned to Us. Then He, may His praise be exalted, informed them of what He has prepared, of His honour in His presence, for those among them who are patient in obeying Him, saying: ﴿And those who believed﴾, meaning: those who affirmed God and His Messenger in what came to them from God. ﴿And did righteous deeds﴾ means: and acted upon what God commanded them, so they obeyed Him in it, and refrained from what He forbade them. ﴿We will surely settle them in lofty chambers in Paradise﴾ means: We will surely lodge them in Paradise in high chambers.

The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿la-nubawwi'annahum﴾ with the letter bā' (to settle them), while the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it with the letter thā' ﴿la-nathwiyannahum﴾.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are well-known recitations among the reciters of the regions, and scholars among the reciters have recited each of them; their meanings are close. Whichever of the two a reader recites is correct. This is because His saying ﴿la-nubawwi'annahum﴾ comes from "bawwa'tuhu manzilan," meaning I settled him in a dwelling; and likewise ﴿la-nathwiyannahum﴾ comes from "athwaytuhu maskanan," when I lodged him in a dwelling, from ath-thawa' (abiding), which is residence.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾

He says: beneath their trees the rivers flow. ﴿Abiding therein forever﴾ means: remaining in them without end. ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾ means: how excellent is the recompense of those who work by obeying God, these chambers which God lodges them in His gardens, beneath which rivers flow; those who were patient over the harm of the polytheists in this world, and what they encountered from them, and in acting upon obedience to God and what pleases Him, and in striving against His enemies. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾ regarding their provision and their struggle against their enemies, so they do not shrink back from them, trusting that God will make His word supreme and weaken the plot of the disbelievers, and that what has been apportioned to them of provision will never escape them.

As for His saying: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 62–63:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants, and restricts it for him. Indeed Allah is Knowing of everything.﴾ (62)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Allah widens the provision of whomever He wills of His creation, and constricts it, restricting it for whomever He wills among them. He means: your provisions and their distribution among you, O people, are in My hand, apart from anyone else besides Me. I extend it to whomever I will, and restrict it for whomever I will. * *

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: And if you asked these polytheists among your people, O Muhammad, "Who sends down water from the sky," meaning the rain which Allah sends down from the clouds, ﴿and thereby gives life to the earth﴾ means: and thereby gives life to the earth by the water that came down from the sky. Its giving life is its causing plants to grow in it, ﴿after its death﴾ means after its barrenness and dryness.

* *

His saying: ﴿They would surely say, "Allah"﴾

He means: They would surely say that the One who did that is Allah, the One to whom all things are worshipped.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: When Allah delivered these polytheists from what they were in at sea, from fear and dread of drowning, to the land, behold, after they had reached the land they associate with Allah gods and rivals. ﴿So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them﴾ means: so that they may deny the blessing of Allah which He bestowed upon them in their persons and their property.

﴿And so that they may enjoy themselves﴾: The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read ﴿wa-liyatamatta'u﴾ with a kasra on the lam, meaning: and in order that they may enjoy what We have given them. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿wa-l-yatamatta'u﴾ with a sukun on the lam, in the sense of threat and reproach: that is, disbelieve, for you will soon know what punishment of Allah you will meet because of your disbelief in Him.

The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of those who read it with a sukun on the lam, in the sense of threat and warning. This is because those who read it with a kasra on the lam claimed that they chose the kasra by way of coordinating it with the lam in His saying ﴿li-yakfuru﴾, and that since ﴿li-yakfuru﴾ means "in order that they disbelieve," the correct form of ﴿wa-liyatamatta'u﴾ would be "and in order that they enjoy," as it is coordinated with ﴿li-yakfuru﴾ in their view. But what they went in that direction is not sound. This is because the lam in ﴿li-yakfuru﴾ can carry the meaning of "in order that," since it expresses a purpose: it means that when they associate others with Allah, it is in order that they disbelieve in the blessings We gave them. That is not the case with ﴿wa-liyatamatta'u﴾, because their associating others with Allah was disbelief in His blessing, and their associating others with Him was not enjoyment of this world, although associating others with Him does facilitate for them the path to enjoying it. Since that is the case, directing it to the sense of threat is more appropriate and more fitting than directing it to the sense of "and in order that they enjoy." Furthermore, it has been mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy it is ﴿wa-tamatta'u﴾, and that is evidence for the soundness of the one who read it with a sukun on the lam in the sense of warning.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And who is more unjust, O people, than one who invents a lie against Allah, saying, when they commit an indecency: "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah commanded us to do it," and "Allah does not command indecency." ﴿Or denies the truth when it has come to him﴾ means: or denies what Allah sent His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ with, of His oneness and of disavowing the idols and rivals, when this truth had come to him from Allah. ﴿Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?﴾ means: Is there not in the Fire a residence and dwelling for whoever disbelieves in Allah, denies His oneness, and denies His Messenger ﷺ? This is an affirmation (taqrir), not a question; it is like the saying of Jarir:

*Are you not the best of those who rode the mounts,*
*And the most generous of all peoples in the palms of hand?*[[The verse is by Jarir ibn Atiyah al-Khatafi, from a poem praising Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan (his Diwan, Sawi edition, Cairo, p. 98). Al-mataya is the plural of mattiyya, meaning camels on whose backs one rides during journeys. Al-rah is the plural of rahah, the palm of the hand. The verse is cited by the author and by Abu Ubayda as evidence that the interrogative here is meant as taqrir, not a true question. Taqrir: compelling the addressee to acknowledge and confess to what is asked about. Abu Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an, folio 186a, at His saying "Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?": its figurative sense is that of affirmation, because this alif may be used for interrogation or for affirmation, and here it is for affirmation. Jarir said, "Are you not..." the verse, and he was not in doubt; rather, he asserted to them that they were so, and had they not been, they would not have rewarded him. A man rebukes his servant and says, "Did you do such-and-such?" while not doubting. It is related that when Abd al-Malik heard this verse, he answered it by saying: "Yes, we are so."]]

He only informs that for those who disbelieve in Allah there is a dwelling in the Fire, and an abode in which they will reside.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 69:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who strive for Us—We will surely guide them to Our paths. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And those who fought these people who fabricate lies against Allah, from the disbelievers of Quraysh, who denied the truth when it came to them, concerning Us, seeking by their fighting the elevation of Our word and the victory of Our religion, ﴿We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾"—meaning: We will grant them success in reaching the straight way, which is attaining the religion of Allah, that is Islam, with which Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good﴾—meaning: And indeed Allah is with those of His creation who do good, those who strive in Him against the people of polytheism, affirming His Messenger in what he brought from Allah, by aiding him and giving him victory over those of his enemies he fought.

And in agreement with what we have said concerning the interpretation of His saying, ﴿And those who strive for Us﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said:

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying, ﴿And those who strive for Us﴾: I said to him, "They fought for Us?" He said, "Yes."

End of the tafsir of Surah al-'Ankabut.
